title: AI and OCR Privacy Review Checklist

checks.question: Does the provider request contain only fields required for the named AI or OCR capability?
checks.expected: The review lists every transmitted field, its purpose, and why processing cannot use a less sensitive representation.
requiredEvidence: negative test proving unrelated fields are omitted
blockingConditions: a transmitted field has no documented purpose
a whole domain object is serialized instead of an allowlisted request
confirmed financial records are sent when suggestion input is sufficient

checks.question: Are provider retention, training, subprocessors, processing region, deletion, access, encryption, and incident terms answered and approved?
checks.expected: The provider review records default and configurable retention, model-training use, subprocessors, cross-border region, encryption, support access, deletion SLA, and incident notification.
requiredEvidence: current provider terms or data-processing agreement
blockingConditions: retention or model-training use is unknown
subprocessor or processing-region information is unavailable
deletion capability or incident notification is not documented

checks.question: Are unnecessary identifiers and metadata removed before content crosses the provider boundary?
checks.expected: The integration omits or irreversibly redacts unrelated identifiers, strips unnecessary file metadata, and validates the minimized payload before transmission.
requiredEvidence: negative test proving prohibited fields are absent
blockingConditions: reversible encoding is treated as redaction
receipt metadata is transmitted without a capability need
raw account, session, or confirmed-record identifiers are exposed

checks.question: Is raw AI or OCR input confined to approved service-owned storage with opaque references and bounded retention?
checks.expected: Raw prompts, receipt bytes, and OCR text stay in encrypted owner storage only when required; events, drafts, logs, tickets, and evidence use opaque references or safe metadata.
blockingConditions: raw input is copied into an integration event or transaction draft
retention has no bounded duration or deletion path
another service reads owner storage without an authenticated authorization boundary

checks.question: Do logs, metrics, traces, failure events, and operator evidence exclude sensitive AI and OCR content?
checks.expected: Observability uses stable technical identifiers, safe categories, attempts, durations, and timestamps without prompts, receipt content, OCR text, provider payloads, exception details, or financial values.
blockingConditions: request or response bodies are logged
provider exception messages or payloads reach shared telemetry
raw content appears in Jira, Confluence, dashboards, or alerts

checks.question: Does the user experience obtain required consent and disclose external AI or OCR processing before transmission?
checks.expected: The privacy policy and consent flow identify the processing purpose, provider category, data classes, retention or deletion expectations, cross-border processing where applicable, withdrawal path, and non-provider fallback.
blockingConditions: provider processing starts before required consent
the privacy policy omits external processing
withdrawal leaves no safe manual or provider-disabled path

checks.question: Do automated tests, fixtures, demos, and troubleshooting artifacts use only synthetic or irreversibly sanitized data?
checks.expected: Receipt images, OCR text, prompts, provider responses, identities, and financial values are generated for tests and cannot be traced to a real person or production record.
blockingConditions: a fixture originated from a production export or real receipt
real provider prompts or responses are committed
screenshots or logs contain personal or financial data

checks.question: Can provider access be disabled and stored provider data be deleted without creating an authoritative financial side effect?
checks.expected: Credentials can be revoked, provider processing can fail closed, deletion requests are traceable, and provider output remains untrusted suggestion data.
blockingConditions: disabling a provider exposes raw content or silently confirms a record
provider-held data has no deletion or escalation path
provider output bypasses deterministic validation and user confirmation
